summary: Aptus is a rapidly growing branded-formulations marketer, not an established integrated manufacturer. FY2026 revenue reached ₹46.57 crore, but four consecutive reported years consumed operating cash. At the dated October19 secondary close of ₹482.10, the verified post-bonus 1.715 crore shares imply ₹826.80 crore equity value, approximately 179 times FY2026 PAT on the current share base. Strong growth and a proposed manufacturing investment do not make this an inexpensive stock. The cash-funded reference produces a terminal price of ₹153.08 and −20.50% annual return; even the substantial bull reaches only ₹464.32 and −0.75%. The assessed classification is weak setup / value-trap risk, not an allegation about the issuer. A material price or cash-economics change would be needed before the present model offers a reasonable return. This is general research conditional on a ₹5 lakh reference position, not a personal allocation recommendation.

sections.title: Executive assessment and investment decision
sections.text: Aptus is a rapidly growing branded-formulations marketer, not an established integrated manufacturer. FY2026 revenue reached ₹46.57 crore, but four consecutive reported years consumed operating cash. At the dated October19 secondary close of ₹482.10, the verified post-bonus 1.715 crore shares imply ₹826.80 crore equity value, approximately 179 times FY2026 PAT on the current share base. Strong growth and a proposed manufacturing investment do not make this an inexpensive stock. The cash-funded reference produces a terminal price of ₹153.08 and −20.50% annual return; even the substantial bull reaches only ₹464.32 and −0.75%. The assessed classification is weak setup / value-trap risk, not an allegation about the issuer. A material price or cash-economics change would be needed before the present model offers a reasonable return. This is general research conditional on a ₹5 lakh reference position, not a personal allocation recommendation.

sections.title: Identity, accounting scope and four gates
sections.text: Aptus Pharma Limited, formerly Aptus Pharma Private Limited, was incorporated August12,2010, converted to public status December12,2024 and listed on BSE SME September30,2025. ISIN INE15XJ01010; BSE544529/APPL. The FY2026 accounts are standalone Indian Accounting Standards under the older AS framework, not Ind AS; there is no subsidiary, associate or joint venture. A stray benefit-policy reference to Ind AS19 does not convert the financial-reporting framework. G1 Integrity is Conditional: no verified fraud or default finding, but product-liability allocation, reporting consistency and connected-party oversight matter. G2 Reliability is Conditional: the later audited annual statements provide the most detailed reconciled hierarchy; cash-flow presentation differences and issue-cost scope remain expressly qualified, not ignored. G3 Funding is Conditional: the models do not assume the proposed capital has arrived and explicitly fund shortfalls. G4 Tradability is Conditional: the observed history supports a finite reference calculation, but frequent one-price sessions, a large lot and unverified live BSE restrictions prevent an assurance of execution.

sections.title: Canonical scores, confidence and audit
sections.text: The assessed factors are GOV5, MOAT4, REV8, DUR6, CAP6, CASH2, BAL5, EXEC5 and EARN6; investment factors are R1, D1, P1 and L5. BQS is5.08. Raw Growth Quality is6.40, capped at5.00 for persistent CASH2. IAS is0.25×5.08+0.35×1+0.20×1+0.10×1+0.10×5=2.42. REV mechanically reaches the9 growth band, but Medium evidence confidence caps it at 8 under framework section3. Six observations do not override the confidence requirement. All historical factor inputs have Medium confidence; forecast uncertainty is separately substantial. No factor is filled with a neutral placeholder or reweighted. The cash-conversion cap is not a finding of misconduct, and neither the corrected AGM table nor the withdrawn court petition is treated as an automatic integrity failure.

sections.title: Business model, products and revenue quality
sections.text: The business develops and promotes branded generic formulations through doctors, distributors and a sales network. Manufacturing is outsourced to WHO-GMP-described counterparties; current ownership of a factory is not established. The August presentation describes two formal loan-licence manufacturing arrangements and other purchase-order suppliers. FY2025 procurement involved seven contract manufacturers, with average60-day order lead times and no universal long-term or exclusive supply protection. FY2026 has250-plus formulations and91 employees, versus194 products in FY2025 and140 in FY2023. Reported gross product sales ₹40.9243 crore plus commission/service revenue ₹6.9046 crore, less product returns ₹1.2543 crore, reconcile to ₹46.5746 crore net sales. Service revenue was only ₹1.3652 crore in FY2025. Direct foreign-currency earnings are nil; domestic merchant-export arrangements and commission are not direct export sales. Returns rose from1.63% to3.06% of gross product sales. Product count is not proof of differentiated patents, recurring prescriptions or a quantified addressable market.

sections.title: Industry, competition and economic moat
sections.text: Prescription-led demand and chronic therapies offer repeat usage, while consumer-health and OTC products can broaden distribution. But competition is intense, doctor access must be continually maintained, generic substitution is possible and quality/licensing problems can interrupt sales. Product permissions and development ₹1.2411 crore and sales promotion ₹6.9550 crore were expensed in FY2026, against ₹0.4504 crore and ₹3.0020 crore in the annual comparative. The selling effort is real and recurring, not a free intangible moat. FY2025 largest-customer/top-five/top-ten shares were8.83%/32.74%/48.84%, down from14.33%/47.09%/68.37% in FY2023; improvement is positive, but FY2026 customer percentages were not verified. Prospectus peers are Sunrest, Lincoln and Zota, explicitly imperfect comparisons. Zota’s primary FY2026 presentation describes a large company-operated/franchise pharmacy network and export manufacturing, materially different from Aptus’s present sales-led model. Its old headline multiple is not transplanted into Aptus. No updated peer price multiple is claimed without matching current capital, earnings and scope.

sections.title: Historical financial reconstruction and per-share bridge
sections.text: Revenue/PAT in ₹crore were FY2021 5.0958/0.0383, FY2022 10.5067/0.1008, FY2023 13.8973/0.1943, FY2024 17.8570/0.7981, FY2025 24.5577/3.0996 and FY2026 46.5746/4.6199. FY2021–22 are original statutory figures from a statement denominated in rupees in hundreds; FY2023–25 use the later prospectus restatement, and FY2026 uses the annual report. Older figures are not silently represented as subsequently restated. Five-year sales CAGR is55.66%, from a very small base; FY2026 sales rose89.65% while PAT rose49.05%, compressing PAT margin from12.62% to9.92%. Core EBIT excludes other income and adds only actual borrowing interest, retaining bank/processing charges as an economic cost: FY2023–26 approximately₹0.3940/1.2530/4.4130/6.9617 crore. Depreciation FY2026 is₹0.4080 crore. The annual EPS₹7.78 is weighted and pre-May-bonus; it is not comparable with the current quoted share denomination without adjustment. Current issued-share PAT per share is₹2.69. IPO added18.60 lakh shares, then the May12 3:2 bonus took 68.60 lakh to 171.50 lakh shares without cash. The proposed preferential issue would add 16.0287 lakh only upon actual allotment; the matched alternative includes its cash and shares together.

sections.title: Cash conversion, working capital and forensic reconciliation
sections.text: Reported FY2023–26 CFO was−₹0.1810/−2.1746/−1.8382/−5.6028 crore. Three-year cumulative CFO/PAT is−112.89%; the four-year measure is−112.45%. FY2026 CFO less cash PPE purchases is−₹7.7892 crore, before the additional ₹4.3181 crore investing movement in other noncurrent assets, principally bank deposits rather than manufacturing construction. Receivables grew from₹5.6394 to18.7601 crore and inventory from₹7.0580 to13.5688 crore; payables grew₹6.8441 crore, financing part of the increase. Closing receivable days rose to about147 and inventory is about232 days of cost of goods sold using the closing stock; average-balance ratios differ. Receivables are classified good:₹18.5524 crore under six months overdue and₹0.2076 crore six–twelve months, with none older than one year; no independently verified later collection ledger or inventory-expiry ageing was obtained. The annual cash flow differs from the April results, which showed CFO−₹6.8597 crore, but both close at₹1.0271 crore cash and the balance-sheet totals agree. The annual gives the detailed current/noncurrent and deposit classifications and is used consistently. Negative rows labelled proceeds and positive rows labelled repayment are tested against the debt decrease₹3.1752 crore, not read literally. The historical cash-flow weakness survives either CFO presentation, so the conclusion does not depend on choosing the worse version.

sections.title: Governance, related parties and legal record
sections.text: Promoters held72.89% after the bonus in the August14 reference; the proposed issue would reduce this to67.19%, not67.18%. September7’s corrigendum adds the complete allottee ownership table and fixes that rounding discrepancy without changing the aggregate issue, price or objects. It includes promoter-group allottees; it is not an all-public issue. MD remuneration rose from₹8.40 lakh to₹22.80 lakh, with an independently disclosed171.53% increase; the absolute amount is about4.94% of PAT, not a majority-profit extraction claim. The annual also lists CEO/CFO/CS payments and₹22.39 lakh to three managerial relatives. Related Janta Drug Agency sales were₹84.82 lakh, about1.82% of sales, versus₹138.43 lakh previously. Related loans fell from₹1.1140 to₹0.2383 crore after₹1.7261 crore repayments and₹0.8504 crore additions; the closing balance is in debt. The FY2026 auditor issued unmodified financial/internal-control opinions and reported no observed audit-trail tampering or loan default, within its audit scope. These are not blanket governance assurances. The prospectus discloses FDC Limited’s ELECTUS ORS trademark suit, an interim restraint and a July29,2025 joint settlement application; a final disposal order was not independently verified. Aptus’s separate Delhi High Court WP(C)8726/2023 challenged the chlorpheniramine-maleate/codeine combination prohibition. The court’s actual January13,2026 order names Aptus and dismisses the petitions and applications as withdrawn. This supersedes the stale prospectus description of an ongoing petition; withdrawal is neither a merits finding against Aptus nor permission for new manufacture. The prospectus’s ₹17,730 personal tax demand concerns a promoter, not an issuer liability. Manufacturer agreements lacked predetermined product-liability indemnity allocation; no resulting company liability is asserted merely from that contractual risk.

sections.title: Capital allocation, funding and complete opening-claim map
sections.text: FY2026 equity is₹23.3462 crore and debt₹7.1816 crore. Cash is₹1.0271 crore, plus₹5.3861 crore noncurrent bank deposits. The note specifically states₹1.14 lakh of deposits is pledged; the reference uses that literal₹0.0114 crore and releases the remainder during FY2027, with all-deposits-blocked and delayed-release sensitivities. This does not treat noncurrent deposits as instant distributable cash. CARE and the annual report say the₹13.02 crore IPO is fully used:₹1.6295 crore office/racks,₹8 crore working capital,₹1.9105 crore general purposes and₹1.48 crore issue expenses. The equity note charges₹1.2598 crore issue expenses, reconciling to net cash issuance₹11.7601 crore; CARE includes₹0.63 crore reimbursement within its₹1.48 crore. The₹0.2202 crore scope difference is not fully explained, but no second IPO cash pot, invented future issue bill or misuse finding is inserted. Opening operating WC₹22.956 crore includes trade, all₹2.734 crore ordinary statutory/customer/expense liabilities,₹0.0227 crore current benefits,₹0.034 crore other current provisions and₹0.3612 crore legacy noncurrent gratuity. Future closing WC uses the same broad scope; future service expense is funded through margins, so no second terminal gratuity deduction is made. Current income-tax provision₹1.7022 crore is excluded from WC and settled once. Government assets₹1.1607 crore are not clearly split by tax type, so they remain in operating WC; a separate all-income-tax sensitivity removes them from opening WC and recovers them once in FY2028. No unsupported netting or duplicate recovery occurs. Current loan maturities₹0.2127 crore and remaining NBFC debt₹0.2833 crore are amortized separately;₹0.2383 crore interest-free related debt is assumed repaid FY2028, an estimate not a legal maturity.

sections.title: Returns on capital and growth-quality diagnosis
sections.text: Normalized FY2026 NOPAT is approximately₹5.1865 crore after a25.5% analytical cash-tax rate. Average operating invested capital, defined as equity plus debt less cash, nonoperating deposits and deferred-tax assets plus the tax liability excluded from operating funding, supports about27.43% latest ROIC. Three-year incremental NOPAT divided by incremental similarly defined capital is21.26%, above an analytical13–17% operating cost-of-capital range. Earlier years were much less profitable. Uncertainty over legacy deposit encumbrance and tax-asset composition means these are analytical estimates rather than issuer ratios, and the model separately tests those cash scopes. This supports CAP6, not an automatic exceptional score: recent accounting returns are promising, but four-year operating cash deficits, high inventory/receivable intensity and external capital dependence impede self-funded compounding. Product development is expensed rather than capitalized, which avoids one common profit-inflation mechanism. The manufacturing proposal is a new return cohort whose licensing, utilization, yield and realized cash returns have not yet been demonstrated.

sections.title: Growth runway, plans and execution tests
sections.text: The core runway is wider doctor/distributor coverage, more formulations and repeat chronic/acute demand. Management also intends consumer-health, merchant-export services,20% own manufacturing by2028 and a pan-India footprint by2029. These are plans, not installed capacity or contracted orders. June’s₹51 crore funding concept used₹35 crore equity,₹10 crore debt and₹6 crore accruals; the later equity proposal is₹44.88036 crore at₹280 per share. Its stated objects are₹25 crore land/plant structure/high-tech storage/vehicles,₹10 crore working capital and₹9.88 crore general purposes over36 months, subject to the stated flexibility. The September AGM/corrigendum establishes authorization, not money received; no subsequent executed allotment was verified and the dated master retains17.15 million shares. The reference therefore retains the current outsourced business and no proposed cash or factory. A matched alternative receives the proposed cash, adds every proposed share, estimates1% issue costs and spends₹25 crore over three years, without pretending an inauguration or approval establishes commercial production. Base annual sales₹62/80/100/120/140 crore are already ambitious; success requires cash collection, repeat prescriptions and supplier capacity, not just product launches.

sections.title: Financed annual scenarios, valuation and downside
sections.text: The model starts with audited March2026 stocks and forecasts FY2027–31 plus a202/365 FY2032 stub to October19,2031, an exact five-year investor horizon from the dated quote. April–October activity is estimated, not presented as a verified current balance sheet. Base annual sales are₹62/80/100/120/140/160 crore, EBIT margin15%, operating WC55% of annual revenue, ordinary capex2.5% of sales and terminal15×NOPAT. Bear is₹48/50/53/56/60/64 crore at10% margin,70% WC and10×; bull₹75/105/145/190/245/300 crore at17–18% margin,45% WC and20×. All include annual interest, tax, capex, depreciation, working-capital funding, loan repayment and residual debt. The₹5 crore cash-credit limit plus existing₹2 crore demand borrowing is rolled conditionally, not enlarged by an unexecuted board proposal. Interest11% is solved with half-year new borrowing/repayment, with17% stress reflecting expensive NBFC debt. Minimum operating cash₹1 crore and pledged deposits are not distributed at terminal. Unfunded gaps issue hypothetical equity at70% of the dated quote with5% costs: base needs₹7.4351 crore gross. Capital availability at that price is not guaranteed and may flatter old holders when the market price exceeds modeled value, so₹100/50/25 issue-price sensitivities are also provided. Base terminal₹153.08 gives−20.50% annualized and₹76.11 entry for a15% hurdle; bear₹26.59 gives−43.98%; bull₹464.32 gives−0.75%. Severe terminal₹2.10 is about 99.6% principal loss. In the matched proposed-issue/factory path, base₹152.39/−20.57%, bear₹35.03/−40.81% and bull₹440.33/−1.80%; cash and dilution always travel together. These are scenarios, not target-price promises.

sections.title: Reverse valuation, sensitivities and multibagger test
sections.text: At the base funded path, a15% return requires about94.33× terminal NOPAT instead of15×. Alternatively, fixing the base margin, WC, multiple and hypothetical issue price, the first solved growth route after FY2027 is approximately99.94% annually to₹1,980.89 crore FY2032 annual revenue and₹574.40 crore gross additional equity. This is an extreme reverse-expectations calculation, not a credible forecast or unique solution. Neither5× nor10× investor value is reached in the tested0–120% annual growth range under those fixed financing assumptions; extrapolation is not evidence for a multibagger. Base return stays near−20.5% when all deposits are blocked, or interest is17%;70% WC reduces it to about−21.27%. The matched factory-cost₹35 crore alternative is about−21.03%. A₹5 crore nonrecoverable receivable/inventory stress reduces opening recoverable WC, restores required operating WC through the forecast cash bridge and charges noncash P&L once; it is not a paper write-off plus a second fictitious cash payment. The separate hypothetical₹5 crore legal cash claim is a sensitivity, not an assessed liability. Lower fundraising prices worsen dilution, and the very negative entry economics are not rescued by a minor tax/netting assumption.

sections.title: Liquidity, implementation and final classification
sections.text: All60 BSE reference sessions July24–October19 have observed rows; no missing date is silently filled with zero. The sample follows the May bonus, and no other in-sample capital action was verified. Calculated low×volume turnover bounds average₹51.49 lakh and have median₹42.135 lakh over60 sessions;20-session average/median are₹69.00/56.63 lakh. Using the conservative60-session median, a₹5 lakh reference exit is2.37 days at5% participation,5.93 at2% and1.19 at10%. These are turnover-capacity illustrations, not order-book promises. Twenty-five of60 sessions had identical daily high and low, and several latest sessions show2% moves; direction and future ability to buy or sell are not assumed. Starting L7 is reduced to5 for one-price/circuit-like trading, concentration and a400-share lot costing₹1,92,840. The ₹5 lakh reference is roughly2.59 lots, not an exactly executable order size. Current live spread/depth and comprehensive BSE ASM/GSM/ESM status were not independently established; NSE alert absence is not BSE clearance. Conditional numerical IAS2.42 is therefore not an instruction to trade. BQS5.08 and capped GQS5.00 do not offset the entry-price and permanent-loss exposure: weak setup / value-trap risk.

sections.title: Monitoring, falsification conditions and evidence limits
sections.text: The thesis would improve with verified cash collections, lower inventory intensity and repeated positive CFO after growth funding, together with a materially less demanding entry price. Verify actual preferential allotment/bank receipt and post-issue capital before using the expansion path; obtain capex contracts, land/title and manufacturing permissions, commissioning and output rather than targets. Reconcile the issue-cost scope and original-versus-annual CFO presentation; obtain the government-asset tax split, bank deposit maturity/lien confirmation and updated financing sanctions. Track promoter/related balances, product quality/returns, manufacturer indemnity arrangements and final trademark settlement terms. The court withdrawal is verified; it is not a live manufacturing licence. The announced October20 half-year-results meeting was identified, but no resulting H1 FY2027 statement had been verified at this review cut-off; incorporate it before treating March-based estimates as current fundamentals. Older original and restated historical scopes are labelled; a complete independently reconstructed FY2021–22 cash-flow series was not established, so the cash-conversion assessment uses the four verified later years. Live executable liquidity, current exhaustive surveillance status, full inventory ageing and post-year-end customer receipts remain unavailable. These limitations bound the conclusions rather than being replaced by invented reassuring facts.

gates.reason: Scoped unmodified audit and no verified fraud/default finding; related-party, contractual product-liability and disclosure consistency risks remain. Verified court withdrawal is not a merits conviction.

Use later audited annual hierarchy with explicit original-result CFO and IPO-cost scope discrepancies. Balance-sheet/cash totals and financing bridges reconcile; ranges do not alter the very weak valuation conclusion. No unresolved critical reliability failure is asserted.

Negative cash conversion requires explicit funding. Reference includes only existing finance and hypothetical priced equity; proposed preferential cash appears only with matched shares and spending. Loan rollover and capital availability are not guaranteed.

Verified sample identity/calendar and post-bonus share/lot bridge support a conditional turnover-bound test. Frequent one-price sessions and missing live spread/depth/BSE surveillance verification require execution checks, not an invented no-trade prohibition.

limitations: No verified H1 FY2027 results from the October20 meeting at the review cut-off; April–October balance-sheet changes are modeled estimates.
Final voting results, preferential allotment and receipt were not independently verified; the proposal and proceedings are not execution.
Government-asset tax composition, exact deposit maturity/encumbrance confirmation and IPO-cost scope not fully resolved; explicit sensitivities provided.
Inventory expiry ageing, post-year-end collections and final trademark settlement disposal not independently verified.
BSE turnover uses secondary OHLCV bounds; no live depth/spread or exhaustive current BSE surveillance clearance.
FY2021–22 original statutory history is not a reconstructed/restated cash-flow series.

Verify executed preferential allotment, received funds, updated shares, bank sanctions and capex commitments.
Reconcile cash-flow presentation and issue-cost scope; obtain tax-asset, deposit and ageing confirmations.
Recheck live BSE lot/restrictions/order book before any position-specific implementation assessment.
